_comment: Curated mapping from decoded-label fields to Brick Schema classes, used by src/brick/. Same doctrine as deterministic_rules.json: every entry cites its source, unknown maps to the generic base class (Point / Equipment / System) -- NEVER invent a more specific class. Cited as brick_mapping.json:<section>.<key>. Every class name here must exist in knowledge_base/brick_dir/brick_classes.txt (enforced by tests/test_brick_mapping.py).

system_prefix_class._comment: First 2 digits of the 4-digit NS 3451 code -> Brick system class.

31._source: TFM 310 Sanitaerinstallasjoner; conservative: NS 31xx covers cold + hot + drainage (the pilot's 310 lesson, CLAUDE.md sec 3), so no Domestic_Hot_Water claim from the code alone

32._source: TFM 320 Varmeanlegg; medium data-confirmed as water (data_observations.md: Tasen 320001 heating supply r=-0.80 vs outdoor)

43._source: TFM 43x elkraft fordeling (CLAUDE.md sec 3: 4320/4330/4340 electrical distribution)

point_class_rules._source: AO/BO object types and kommando decodes (deterministic_rules.json:command_object_types)

point_class_rules._comment: Ordered list, FIRST match wins (so Temperature_Setpoint beats Temperature_Sensor). No match -> Point: never invent a class.

equipment_letter_class._comment: NS 3457-8 component letters -> Brick equipment class, for tokens that name a whole device (equipment tokens / same_equipment group keys).

IK._source: IK = Kuldeaggregat (komponentkodeliste.md line 309) DELIBERATELY generic: the code covers Kjolemaskin, Frysemaskin AND Varmepumpe -- claiming Chiller would over-claim; needs per-point evidence

equipment_token_class._comment: Case-insensitive substring of an equipment token -> Brick class, for tokens without NS letters.

pumpe._source: Norwegian 'pumpe' in equipment tokens like Spillvannspumpe_P2 / Drenspumpe_P1 (bacnet_sd_label_grammar.md glossary)

unit_map._comment: Decoded unit string -> QUDT unit local name (http://qudt.org/vocab/unit/). NOK (cost) has no QUDT energy unit -> unmapped.

ppm._source: QUDT unit vocabulary, parts per million
